cards.text: This letter skips the “hope this finds you well” and jumps STRAIGHT in. The writer never signs his name, and he never names his readers either, he just writes straight to “you.” He opens with “That which was from the beginning,” and friend, he's got a LOT to say about it.

cards.question: The writer says he only heard about this from other people, secondhand.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: NO sir, this man heard it, SAW it, gazed at it and TOUCHED it with his own hands, and he calls it the Word of life. He's not forwarding some rumor from the group chat, friend, he was standing RIGHT THERE.
That life was revealed: the eternal life that was with the Father showed up where the writer and the others with him could actually SEE it. No blurry photo, no “trust me, you had to be there.”

cards.question: The writer and the others with him have seen this eternal life up close. What do they do with it?

answers.text: They testify to it and proclaim it
They keep it quiet among themselves
They wait for the right time to share it

cards.question: The writer and the others with him proclaim what they've seen and heard to the readers. Why?

answers.text: So the readers can have fellowship with them
So the readers can earn a place among them
So the readers can prove they are worthy

cards.text: Then the writer tells them who this fellowship of theirs is with. Friend, this is NOT a guest list you skim. This is the kind you read TWICE.

cards.question: Who does the writer say this fellowship of theirs is with?

answers.text: The Father and His Son Jesus Christ
The prophets and the holy angels
The elders and the apostles

cards.question: The writer gives one more reason he and the others write these things. What is it?

answers.text: So that our joy may be complete
So that our names will be remembered
So that our worries may be settled

cards.text: Now the writer gets to the BIG message they heard from Him. And he doesn't make you dig for it like scissors in a junk drawer, he puts it right up front.

cards.question: God is ___, and in Him there is no darkness at all.

answers.text: light
distant
silent

cards.text: So say we claim fellowship with God but keep walking in the darkness. The writer's about to say what that means for us, and friend, I am all EARS. Well. All mustache.

cards.question: What does the writer say about us if we claim fellowship with God but walk in the darkness?

answers.text: We lie and don't practice the truth
We lose the joy we were given
We are cut off and can't return

cards.question: But if we walk in the light as God is in the light, what cleanses us from all sin?

answers.text: The blood of Jesus His Son
The water of the Jordan River
The ashes of a red heifer

cards.question: The writer says that when we walk in the light, we have fellowship with one another.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Next up: saying we have no sin at all. Friend, I shared a junk drawer with dead batteries who SWORE they still had a charge, so I've heard this one before.

cards.question: If we say we have no sin, who does the writer say we're fooling?

answers.text: Ourselves
Our neighbors
Our leaders

cards.text: But there's a better road, and it starts with owning up. Like me walking out holding the burnt tray: “Yeah. That was me.”

cards.question: If we confess our sins, what does the writer say God does?

answers.text: He forgives us and cleanses us
He forgives us but keeps a record
He waits until we prove ourselves

cards.question: The writer comes back to the claim one more time. If we say we have not sinned, what do we make God out to be?

answers.text: A liar
A stranger
A bystander

cards.text: Then he goes soft and calls them “My little children,” and he says he's writing so they won't sin. But if anyone does, they are NOT on their own.

cards.question: But if anyone does sin, who does the writer say is our advocate before the Father?

answers.text: Jesus Christ the Righteous One
Moses the servant of God
Michael the archangel

cards.text: And Jesus doesn't just speak up for us. He Himself is the atoning sacrifice for our sins.

cards.question: The writer says Jesus is the atoning sacrifice only for the sins of the people this letter is written to.

answers.text: True
False
